review.raw_markdown:
--- # Skechers.com Mobile Journey Review — Walker Miles **Date:** April 11, 2026 | **Vs. Yesterday's Score: 4/10** --- ## 1. Executive Summary I fired up skechers.com on my phone today hoping to grab a pair of Slip-ins. The Men's navigation was actually pretty solid — I found the Hands Free Slip-ins category without much trouble, landed on a good-looking shoe at a fair price with the BOGO deal. But the experience fell apart at the worst possible moment: the cart page came up completely blank. Nothing. White screen. I had no idea if my shoe was in there or not. On top of that, the homepage greeted me with Mother's Day content wall-to-wall, no sign Skechers knows I'm a guy who's been buying their shoes for years, and when I searched "slip in" the top results were all Women's. Today felt like shopping as a stranger, not as a loyal Plus member. --- ## 2. Business Impact Score: 4/10 Same score as yesterday. The cart failure is a critical regression that stops a sale dead in its tracks. No improvement in homepage personalization or search relevance. --- ## 3. What's Working - **BOGO 50% OFF** is plastered at the top of every page — I noticed it immediately and it's a real motivator for a price-conscious guy like me - **Men's category navigation** is clean and well-spaced. "Hands Free Slip-ins" is right there as a shortcut without digging — that's exactly what I want - **Hands Free Slip-ins landing page** nails it: big clear headline, 263 results, width filters (Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit) front and center, brief tech explanation - **Product page** is readable without zooming. Product name is large, price is visible, the BOGO promo is called out in red, and the Hands-Free Slip-ins badge confirms what I'm looking at - **ADD TO CART button** is large, full-width, high-contrast blue — easy to tap with a big thumb --- ## 4. What's Weak **Cart page is completely blank.** This is the single worst thing I saw today. Step 8 — the cart — rendered as a pure white screen with nothing on it. I tapped ADD TO CART (after the "please select a size" reminder), and then went to view my cart and saw absolutely nothing. Did my shoe make it in? Do I have a BOGO discount applied? Is there a checkout button? I have no idea. At my age I'm not going to dig around troubleshooting a website — I'm going to close the tab. **Homepage doesn't know I exist.** The entire above-the-fold screen is Mother's Day: pink flowers, women in pink shoes, "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love." I'm a 62-year-old guy logged into a Skechers Plus account. Not one piece of men's content, not a single Slip-in, not a "Welcome back, Walker" — nothing. Feels like I landed on the wrong website. **Login captured nothing visible.** Steps 2 and 3 looked identical to the homepage. No confirmation I was logged in, no personalized greeting, no "your Plus benefits are active" acknowledgment. The BOGO deal shows at the top but that's available to everyone. **"Please select a size" is a wall, not a guide.** Step 7 showed an error triangle and the message, but no size was pre-highlighted or suggested. Older shoppers benefit from a little more hand-holding here. **Search returned Women's first.** I searched "slip in" and got 1,026 results — but the two products shown above the fold are both labeled Women's. Zero filtering by my gender, zero personalization from my login. I had to scroll past women's shoes to find what I came for. --- ## 5. Recommendations 1. **Fix the cart page immediately.** A blank cart is an abandoned purchase. This is P0. 2. **Personalize the homepage for logged-in men.** I should see Men's Slip-ins or a "Welcome back" banner, not Mother's Day flowers. 3. **Apply gender context to search.** A logged-in male user searching "slip in" should see Men's results by default, with a clear toggle to switch. 4. **Show login confirmation.** After sign-in, give me a brief "Welcome back, Walker — your Plus benefits are active" message so I know the site knows me. 5. **Pre-select or highlight the most popular size** on the product page, or at minimum animate the size grid when the error fires so my eye goes directly to it. --- ## 6. Bottom Line The bones are there — Men's nav works, the Slip-ins category is easy to find, and the product page is readable. But I couldn't complete a purchase today because the cart was blank, I never felt like a recognized customer, and search put women's shoes in my face. This is a 4/10, same as yesterday. The cart regression alone is enough to keep it from improving. Fix the cart, fix the homepage greeting, fix search defaults — then this gets interesting. --- ## 7. Evidence **Step 1 — Homepage** Landed on a Mother's Day hero image: woman and young girl in pink, pink flowers everywhere, script font. "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love" sub-banner. Not one piece of men's content visible. As a 62-year-old male shopper who's been buying Skechers for years, this felt like I walked into the wrong store. BOGO 50% OFF banner at top was the only thing that kept me interested. The MENU hamburger and nav icons (search, account, cart) are small — had to look carefully to find the account icon. **Step 2 — Dismiss Popups** No popup appeared to dismiss. Screenshot is identical to the homepage. Either no popup was triggered or it was already gone. No friction from a popup, but also no welcome back message — a missed personalization moment. **Step 3 — Log In** Page looks identical to the homepage. No visible login confirmation, no change in the header to show my name or Plus status. The cart badge shows "0" — so if I was logged in, the site didn't surface any account context. Feels anonymous. **Step 4 — Men's Category** This was the highlight of the journey. Clean vertical list: Shoes, Shop by Activity, Comfort Technologies, Collections, Collaborations, Clothing & Accessories — all with adequate row height for tapping. Below the separator: "Hands Free Slip-ins," "Wide Fit," "Extra Wide Fit" as quick shortcuts. Perfect for a guy who knows exactly what he wants. Text is readable, spacing is comfortable. **Step 5 — Men's Shoes (Hands Free Slip-ins)** Exactly where I wanted to be. "Hands Free Slip-ins" as a big H1, tech description below, 263 results count, width filter buttons across the top (Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit, and a third partially cut off). Product grid begins loading at the bottom. This page works well. Filter and Sort by options visible. **Step 6 — View Product** Product: Skechers Slip-ins Max Cushioning Arch Fit 2.0 — Azusah. MEN'S label present. Price $135.00, clearly visible. 4-star rating, 11 reviews. "Buy 1, Get 1 50% OFF! Applied at Cart" in red — immediately caught my eye and made the price feel reasonable. Hands-Free Slip-ins badge confirmed the product type. Large shoe photo. Good readability throughout. **Step 7 — Add to Cart** Size grid was clean — sizes 7.0 through 14.0 in a well-spaced grid, easy to tap. QTY shows 1. "Ship it" and "Check in-store availability" options below. ADD TO CART button is large, full-width, blue — the best touch target on the whole site. However, the page showed "Please select a size" with a warning triangle, meaning no size was selected when the action was attempted. A small friction point but the error message is clear enough. **Step 8 — Cart** Completely blank. White screen. Nothing rendered. This is the single biggest failure in today's journey. After spending time finding the right shoe, confirming it had the BOGO deal, and working through size selection — the cart page showed me nothing. No product, no total, no checkout button. I would have given up here entirely. **Step 9 — Search ("slip in")** Search returned 1,026 results for "SLIP IN" — strong inventory signal. But both products visible above the fold are labeled Women's ("Arch Fit Arcade - See Ya There" and "Contour Foam - Cozy Fit"). As a male, logged-in customer, I should not have to scroll past women's shoes to find men's Slip-ins. No gender filter was applied automatically, no personalization from my account. "Also in Wide" tags were helpful if I could get to men's results, but the default sort undermines the experience. --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Summary Audit covers 8 steps of the mobile purchase funnel on skechers.com (Salesforce Commerce Cloud / Demandware stack). The site carries an unusually heavy third-party script burden, has a functional cart blocker (HTTP 429), a broken third-party widget due to CORS misconfiguration, and 4 critical ARIA violations on the product detail page. LCP and CLS were not captured, leaving core Web Vitals incomplete. --- ## Accessibility **30 axe violations detected; 4 are critical severity.** | Severity | Count | Pages Affected | |----------|-------|----------------| | Critical | 4 | View Product | | Serious | 5+ | Homepage, Men's Shoes, View Product | | Moderate | 15+ | Homepage, Men's Shoes, View Product | | Minor | 1 | Men's Shoes | **Critical violations — require immediate remediation:** - **`image-alt`** (View Product): `` elements missing `alt` attributes. Product images without alt text are both an accessibility failure (WCAG 1.1.1) and a functional loss for screen reader users navigating the PDP. - **`button-name`** (View Product): Buttons with no discernible text. Likely icon-only buttons (size selectors, image carousels) with no `aria-label`. - **`aria-required-children`** (View Product): An element with a role that mandates specific child roles (e.g., `role="listbox"` without `role="option"` children) — indicates broken ARIA widget implementation. - **`aria-valid-attr-value`** (View Product): Invalid ARIA attribute values (e.g., `aria-labelledby` pointing to a non-existent ID). Will silently break assistive technology. **Serious violations:** - **`aria-dialog-name`** (View Product): Modal/dialog overlay missing `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`. Focus management inside modals is likely also broken. - **`aria-input-field-name`** (View Product): Form inputs (size, quantity?) without accessible labels. - **`link-in-text-block`** (Men's Shoes): Links distinguished only by color — fails WCAG 1.4.1 for users with color-vision deficiency. - **`link-name`** (Homepage): Links with no text content — likely icon links in navigation or social links. - **`color-contrast`** (View Product): Foreground/background contrast below 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold. **Structural landmark issues (Homepage, Men's Shoes):** - `landmark-no-duplicate-main` + `landmark-main-is-top-level`: Multiple nested `
